prompt:
This repository is Dispatch, an incident management platform. For some kinds of security cases, Dispatch shuts the case by itself the moment it is opened, before anyone works on it. Which function shuts such a case, and which closing reason does it record on it? Do not change any code.

Finish your answer with these three lines, in this exact form:
FILE: <path of the file that defines that function>
FUNCTION: <name of the function>
REASON: <the closing reason it records>
notes: Answer: src/dispatch/case/flows.py, case_auto_close_flow (called at the end of case_new_create_flow when case.case_type.auto_close), resolution_reason = CaseResolutionReason.user_acknowledged ('User Acknowledged'). Easy: one function, one hop from the case type flag. Lexical gap, grep -i: 'shuts', 'kinds', 'closing reason', 'works on', 'on its own' have 0 hits; 'closing' 6 (eslint config, a closing message string, main.py); 'moment' 20 (the moment.js date library); 'opened' 17; 'record' 73 (participant activity, CLI). The question avoids 'automatic(ally)', which hits the case type edit sheet; the code says auto close and resolution reason. Memory: auto-closing case types are an upstream feature (#5409, Oct 2024); the reason it records is not documented, and a guess would pick Benign or False Positive (the enum holds ten reasons). No plant involved.
